title: Module Overview and Setup
content:
The counting and removal lemmas are the key applications of the Szemerédi Regularity Lemma. This formalization covers three results of increasing generality: the counting lemma for triangles in regular triples, the triangle removal lemma, and the general graph removal lemma.

The formalization works over a finite vertex type `V` with `DecidableEq`, and uses Mathlib's `SimpleGraph` infrastructure throughout.
mathContext: Setting: finite simple graph $G = (V, E)$ with $|V| = n$, $\varepsilon$-regular pairs from Szemerédi's Regularity Lemma.

title: Triangle Count Definition
content:
`triangleCount G A B C` counts ordered triples $(a, b, c) \in A \times B \times C$ forming a triangle in $G$. Implemented via filtering the product set $A \times (B \times C)$ for triples where all three pairs are adjacent.

This counts ordered triples, so each triangle contributes 1 to the count (since vertices are in distinct sets $A$, $B$, $C$). For the counting lemma, this is the natural quantity to estimate.
mathContext: $T(A,B,C) = |\{(a,b,c) \in A \times B \times C : ab, ac, bc \in E(G)\}|$. For random bipartite graphs with densities $d_{12}, d_{13}, d_{23}$, $\mathbb{E}[T] = d_{12} d_{13} d_{23} |A||B||C|$.

title: Counting Lemma
content:
The counting lemma: if $(A, B)$, $(A, C)$, and $(B, C)$ are all $\varepsilon$-regular pairs with edge densities $\geq \varepsilon$, then the triangle count is at least $(d_{AB} - \varepsilon)(d_{AC} - \varepsilon)(d_{BC} - \varepsilon)|A||B||C|$.

The proof idea: for a vertex $a \in A$, its neighborhood in $B$ has size $\approx d_{AB}|B|$ by regularity (for all but $\varepsilon|A|$ vertices). Similarly for $C$. The number of edges between $N(a) \cap B$ and $N(a) \cap C$ is $\approx d_{BC}|N(a) \cap B||N(a) \cap C|$ by regularity of $(B, C)$. Summing over $a$ and handling error terms gives the bound.
mathContext: $T(A,B,C) \geq (d_{AB} - \varepsilon)(d_{AC} - \varepsilon)(d_{BC} - \varepsilon)|A||B||C|$. The error bound is at most $3\varepsilon|A||B||C|$ when densities are $\Theta(1)$.

title: Edge Set Representation
content: `edgeSet G` represents the edges of $G$ as ordered pairs $(v, w)$ where $G.Adj(v, w)$. This representation is used for the removal operation — edges to remove are specified as a subset of these pairs.
mathContext: $E(G) = \{(v,w) \in V \times V : v \sim_G w\}$. Since $G$ is simple, $|E| = 2|E(G)|$ counting ordered pairs.

title: Edge Removal Operation
content:
`removeEdges G R` constructs a subgraph of $G$ by removing all edges in the set $R$. The symmetry proof handles the fact that if $(v, w) \notin R$ we need $(w, v) \notin R$ — this requires the removal set to be symmetric, which is ensured by the `rwa` tactic in the symmetry proof.

This is the key operation for the removal lemma: we need to find a small $R$ that eliminates all triangles.
mathContext: $G' = G \setminus R$ where $v \sim_{G'} w \iff v \sim_G w \wedge (v,w) \notin R$. The goal: $|R| \leq \delta n^2$ and $G'$ is triangle-free.

title: Triangle Removal Lemma (sorry)
content:
For every $\delta > 0$, there exists $\gamma > 0$ such that any graph with at most $\gamma n^3$ triangles can be made triangle-free by removing at most $\delta n^2$ edges.

The proof strategy: (1) Apply the Regularity Lemma with $\varepsilon = \delta/2$ to get a partition. (2) Remove all edges within parts, in irregular pairs, and in regular pairs with density $< \delta/2$. This removes at most $\delta n^2$ edges. (3) Any remaining triangle must have vertices in three mutually regular, dense parts. (4) By the counting lemma, this yields at least $c n^3$ triangles. (5) So if the graph has fewer than $c n^3$ triangles, no such triangle exists and the graph is triangle-free.

The statement uses `True` as a placeholder for the edge count bound, which should be `(Finset.filter ... R).card \leq delta * n^2`.
mathContext: $\forall \delta > 0, \exists \gamma > 0, \forall G$ on $n$ vertices: $T(G) \leq \gamma n^3 \Rightarrow \exists R \subseteq E(G), |R| \leq \delta n^2 \wedge G \setminus R$ is triangle-free.

title: General Graph Removal Lemma (stub)
content:
The general graph removal lemma extends the triangle case to arbitrary subgraphs $H$ on $h$ vertices. The statement: for every $H$ with $h \geq 3$ vertices and every $\delta > 0$, there exists $\gamma > 0$ such that any $G$ with at most $\gamma n^h$ copies of $H$ can be made $H$-free by removing at most $\delta n^2$ edges.

The current formalization is a stub: it only asserts $\exists \gamma > 0$ (proved by $\gamma = 1$) without the actual removal property. The full statement would quantify over all graphs $G$ and assert the removal property.
mathContext: General removal: $\forall H$ on $h$ vertices, $\forall \delta > 0, \exists \gamma > 0$: $\text{copies}(H, G) \leq \gamma n^h \Rightarrow G$ can be made $H$-free by removing $\leq \delta n^2$ edges. Special case $H = K_3$: the triangle removal lemma.

title: Per-Vertex Triangle Contribution and Density Bound
content:
`perVertexTriangles G B C a` counts edges between the $B$-neighborhood and $C$-neighborhood of vertex $a$. The theorem `perVertex_density_bound` establishes: when neighborhoods are $\varepsilon$-fractions of $B$ and $C$, and $(B,C)$ is $\varepsilon$-regular, the per-vertex contribution is at least $(d(B,C) - \varepsilon) \cdot |N_B(a)| \cdot |N_C(a)|$.

This is the inner loop of the counting lemma: for each 'good' vertex $a \in A$ (one with large neighborhoods in both $B$ and $C$), regularity of $(B,C)$ gives a lower bound on the triangle contribution through $a$.

title: Counting Lemma: Full Proof
content:
The complete counting lemma proof. Given $\varepsilon$-regular pairs $(A,B)$, $(A,C)$, $(B,C)$ with densities $\geq \varepsilon$, the triangle count satisfies $T(A,B,C) \geq (d_{AB} - \varepsilon)(d_{AC} - \varepsilon)(d_{BC} - \varepsilon)|A||B||C|$.

The proof structure: (1) Partition $A$ into 'good' vertices (large neighborhoods in both $B$ and $C$) and 'bad' vertices. (2) Show $|\text{bad}| < 2\varepsilon|A|$ using `bad_vertices_small` for both the $(A,B)$ and $(A,C)$ pairs. (3) For each good vertex $a$, apply `perVertex_density_bound` to get $\geq (d_{BC}-\varepsilon)|N_B(a)||N_C(a)|$ triangles through $a$. (4) Use $|N_B(a)| \geq (d_{AB}-\varepsilon)|B|$ and $|N_C(a)| \geq (d_{AC}-\varepsilon)|C|$ from goodness. (5) Sum over good vertices: $T \geq |A_\text{good}| \cdot (d_{AB}-\varepsilon)(d_{AC}-\varepsilon)(d_{BC}-\varepsilon)|B||C|$. (6) Since $|A_\text{good}| \geq (1-2\varepsilon)|A|$, the bound follows.

Also includes `counting_lemma_lower_bound`: a simplified corollary bounding $T \geq c \cdot |A||B||C|$ for positive constant $c$.
mathContext: Full proof: $T(A,B,C) \geq (d_{AB} - \varepsilon)(d_{AC} - \varepsilon)(d_{BC} - \varepsilon)|A||B||C|$ via vertex-by-vertex counting over 'good' vertices with $|A_{\text{good}}| \geq (1-2\varepsilon)|A|$.

title: Triangle Count Monotonicity (Proved)
content:
`triangleCount_mono`: if $A_1 \subseteq A_2$, $B_1 \subseteq B_2$, $C_1 \subseteq C_2$, then $T(A_1,B_1,C_1) \leq T(A_2,B_2,C_2)$. Proved by `Finset.card_le_card`: every triangle in the smaller product is also in the larger product. Corollary `triangleCount_le_total`: $T(A,B,C) \leq T(V,V,V)$ for any subsets.

These monotonicity results are used in the quantitative removal proof to relate per-part triangle counts to total triangle counts.
mathContext: $A_1 \subseteq A_2, B_1 \subseteq B_2, C_1 \subseteq C_2 \Rightarrow T(A_1,B_1,C_1) \leq T(A_2,B_2,C_2)$. Corollary: $T(A,B,C) \leq T(V,V,V)$.

title: Quantitative Triangle Removal via Regularity (Main Result)
content:
The centerpiece of the file: `triangle_removal_quantitative` constructs explicit $\gamma(\delta)$ using the Regularity Lemma. The proof: (1) Set $\varepsilon = \delta/6$ and apply `regularity_with_finpartition` to get a Finpartition with $m_0 \leq k \leq M$ parts. (2) Construct the removal set $R$: edges within parts, edges in irregular pairs, and edges in regular pairs with density $< \delta/2$. (3) Show $|R| \leq \delta n^2$ by counting: within-part edges $\leq n^2/k$, irregular edges $\leq \varepsilon n^2$, sparse edges contribute at most $(\delta/2) n^2$. (4) Show any remaining triangle has vertices in three mutually regular, dense parts (since all other edges were removed). (5) Apply `counting_lemma` to get a positive lower bound on the triangle count from this triple, at least $c \cdot (n/2M)^3$ triangles. (6) Set $\gamma$ small enough that $\gamma n^3 < c(n/2M)^3$, ensuring no such triple exists.

This is the most technically demanding section of the file, requiring careful management of the partition structure (via `Finpartition`), part size bounds (equitability gives $|P_i| \geq n/2M$), and the interplay between the counting lemma and the removal set construction.
mathContext: $\forall \delta > 0$, set $\varepsilon = \delta/6$, $M = M(\varepsilon)$, $\gamma = (\delta/6)^3/(2M)^3$. Then $T(G) \leq \gamma n^3 \Rightarrow \exists R,\, |R| \leq \delta n^2,\, G \setminus R$ triangle-free.
